southern_china.population: general adult population in humid southern regions (estimated 25-45%)

lab_tests: Wood lamp examination (limited utility for dermatophytes)
clinical_features: Moccasin-type (chronic hyperkeratotic, diffuse scaling on soles)

treatment.method: Topical terbinafine 1% cream BID for 1-2 weeks
Topical clotrimazole / miconazole BID for 4 weeks

treatment.indication: Severe, refractory, moccasin-type, or nail involvement

treatment.method: Foot hygiene: keep feet dry, change socks daily, breathable footwear
treatment.indication: All patients — essential for treatment success and recurrence prevention

risk_factors: Public swimming pools, gyms, shared showers
complications: Secondary bacterial infection (cellulitis — especially in diabetic patients)
prevention: Keep feet clean and thoroughly dry (especially between toes)
Change socks daily or more often if sweaty
Alternate shoes to allow complete drying
Use antifungal powder in shoes as prophylaxis if recurrent
Avoid walking barefoot in public wet areas (pools, gyms)

clinical_examples.description: A 40-year-old male construction worker in Shenzhen presents with 2 years of chronic, itchy, scaling feet. Physical exam: diffuse scaling on both soles (moccasin pattern), thick yellowish toenails (great toes bilaterally). KOH prep: numerous septate hyphae. Fungal culture: Trichophyton rubrum.
clinical_examples.key_findings: Chronic moccasin-type tinea pedis + onychomycosis in a patient with occupational risk (closed work boots in humid climate)
clinical_examples.outcome: Prescribed oral terbinafine 250mg daily for 6 weeks (for nail involvement). Advised on foot hygiene: change to moisture-wicking socks, rotate work boots, apply antifungal powder. Follow-up at 12 weeks showed 80% nail clearance and complete skin resolution.

southern_china_humid_areas.population: general adult population in humid southern China (estimated higher due to humidity and allergens)

lab_tests: Clinical diagnosis (no specific lab test required)
Skin prick testing / specific IgE (for trigger identification)
Bacterial culture (if signs of secondary infection)
diagnosis.gold_standard: Clinical diagnosis based on Hanifin & Rajka criteria or UK Working Party diagnostic criteria

treatment.indication: All eczema patients — cornerstone of management

treatment.method: Topical corticosteroids (potency matched to severity and body site)
treatment.indication: Active flare — mild: hydrocortisone 1%, moderate: triamcinolone, severe: clobetasol (short course)
Moderate-severe atopic dermatitis refractory to topicals

risk_factors: Southern China humid climate (sweating, mold exposure)
Family history of atopy (atopic dermatitis, asthma, allergic rhinitis)
Dust mite allergy (major trigger in humid environments)
complications: Eczema herpeticum (HSV superinfection — Kaposi varicelliform eruption)
prevention: Regular emollient use to maintain skin barrier
Avoid known triggers (dust mites, certain foods if confirmed allergic)
Maintain indoor humidity <60% with dehumidifier in southern China

clinical_examples.description: A 6-year-old boy from humid coastal Fujian presents with a 3-year history of recurrent itchy rash in the antecubital and popliteal fossae. Symptoms worsen in summer (sweating, humidity). Family history: father with allergic rhinitis. Exam: erythematous, lichenified plaques in flexural areas with excoriations.
clinical_examples.key_findings: Flexural eczema + seasonal worsening with humidity + family atopic history → atopic dermatitis
clinical_examples.outcome: Intensive emollient therapy + short-course moderate-potency topical corticosteroid (triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID for 7 days). Transitioned to proactive weekend topical corticosteroid for maintenance. Parents advised on humidity control with dehumidifier. Significant improvement at 4-week follow-up.
